Issue #3: WikiLinks: support a display label with `[[Target|Label]]` The `wikilinks` extension always uses the page name as the link text, so `[[Getting Started]]` becomes a link that says "Getting Started". Most wikis (MediaWiki, Obsidian, GitHub wikis) let you write `[[Page name|text to show]]` to link to a page with different text, and our content team keeps writing that out of habit. notes: Labels only accept the same characters as targets ([\w0-9_ -]), so `[[Page|it's]]` or a label with punctuation is left as literal text. This is documented in docs/extensions/wikilinks.md and the issue's examples don't need more. A later change could allow a wider set of characters in labels.
Inside a `tables` row, `[[P|l]]` is split at the pipe into two cells. That is how table parsing already works (block level runs before inline), not a regression, but the docs could mention it.
`[[ | x]]` renders as an empty paragraph, the same as the existing blank-target behaviour for `[[ ]]`.
The test names (test_ac_fr_001_1_...) come from the pipeline's requirement IDs and don't say what each test checks, but this is only cosmetic.
Changelog entry is present under Unreleased > Added. No ARCHITECTURE.md constraints are touched: the change stays inside the extension and the processor priority is unchanged.
